title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
summary: Julian Schrittwieser and colleagues submitted the paper Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model to arXiv on November 19, 2019. The paper presents the MuZero algorithm, which combines tree-based search with a learned model and reports results across Atari, Go, chess, and shogi without being given the underlying environment dynamics or game rules.
significance: A documented reinforcement-learning and planning milestone preserved as a paper-submission event, not as an inferred MuZero system-birth or release date.

verification.note: The original arXiv record establishes the November 19 2019 submission date, authorship, MuZero name, learned-model planning method, and reported Atari/Go/chess/shogi evaluations. Google DeepMind independently describes MuZero as a successor to AlphaZero and states that it mastered chess, Go, shogi, and Atari without needing to be told the rules. This candidate records only the paper-submission milestone and does not infer a separate system-birth date, release date, geography, ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship.
